edit.description: LaneTestsSchema's `lane`: refine against the declared CI lane names the composer is handed
the queue extension the pending gate parses with — hand it `declaration.ci`, which is in scope there

summary: a laneTests[] line's lane is parsed as any non-empty string, so a typo'd or retired lane name is owed forever — never filed, never closed
acceptance: the pending gate refuses a laneTests[] line whose lane no declared CI lane names — the no-`ci` declaration included — while a line naming a declared lane still parses
tests: a laneTests[] line naming a lane the declaration's ci does not carry is refused
a laneTests[] line is refused when the declaration carries no ci at all
pins: a laneTests[] line naming a declared CI lane parses
notes: From a build note. Verified: `lane` is `z.string().min(1)` only; `judge.ts` reports `owedTo` verbatim and the inbox slice keys findings by lane name, so no lane files or closes the line. Fork resolved on the cite's own words ('a declared lane'): refuse unconditionally. `declaration.ci` is `undefined` when none is declared — a readable tri-state at `gates.ts`. Cost: a consumer with a manual second host loses laneTests, which is the mechanism — nothing could close the line.
